classification.difficultyReason: Solve exponential inequalities using logarithms, then interpret strict upper bounds to count positive integer exponents.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Solve $2^x<10^{10}$. How many positive integer powers of 2 are less than $10^{10}$?

answer.short:
$x<\dfrac{10}{\log_{10}2}$ (boundary approximately $33.2$); 33 powers.

The positive integer exponents are $1,2,\ldots,33$.
answer.worked:
Since base 2 is greater than 1, taking logarithms preserves the inequality.
$$\begin{align*}x\log_{10}2&<10\\x&<\frac{10}{\log_{10}2}\end{align*}$$
The exact upper boundary is $\dfrac{10}{\log_{10}2}=33.219280\ldots$. Hence the positive integer exponents are $1,2,\ldots,33$, giving 33 powers.

children.label: b

answer.short:
$x<\dfrac{50}{\log_{10}3}$ (boundary approximately $104.8$); 104 powers.

The positive integer exponents are $1,2,\ldots,104$.
answer.worked:
Since base 3 is greater than 1, taking logarithms preserves the inequality.
$$\begin{align*}x\log_{10}3&<50\\x&<\frac{50}{\log_{10}3}\end{align*}$$
The exact upper boundary is $\dfrac{50}{\log_{10}3}=104.795163\ldots$. Hence the positive integer exponents are $1,2,\ldots,104$, giving 104 powers.
